beats.text: that may be modelled as the direct impact of two bodies.

beats.text: By the end you can choose signed velocities.
beats.caption: Choose signed velocities.

beats.text: Conserve the pair's momentum.
beats.caption: Conserve the pair's momentum.

beats.text: And solve separate and sticking outcomes.
beats.caption: Solve separate and sticking outcomes.

beats.text: Consider two particles moving towards each other along the same straight line on a smooth horizontal surface.
beats.caption: Same straight line

beats.text: They meet. In the first trial, A rebounds and the particles separate.
beats.caption: Trial 1: separate

beats.text: B's dashed arrow is a trial direction. The calculation will decide its signed velocity.
beats.caption: Dashed means an assumed direction

beats.text: Now reset to the original approach. This is a separate trial, with the same initial conditions.
beats.caption: Reset: same initial conditions

beats.text: This time they meet and stick together, or coalesce. We will find their common velocity.
beats.caption: Trial 2: stick together

beats.text: Both trials use a smooth horizontal surface. External horizontal force is negligible during impact. Take right as positive.
Particle A has mass two kilograms
and moves right at four metres per second.
Particle B has mass three kilograms
and moves left at one metre per second.
In trial one, A rebounds left at two metres per second. Find B's final speed and direction.
In the separate sticking trial, find the common velocity. Both questions use the original before diagram. Take a moment to read them.

scenes.title: Why we conserve the pair's momentum

beats.text: Our system is A and B. Weight balances normal reaction; external horizontal force is negligible during impact.
beats.caption: System: A and B together

beats.text: Equal and opposite contact forces are internal. They change the individual momenta in opposite ways.
beats.caption: Equal and opposite internal forces

beats.text: The changes cancel for the pair, so total momentum before equals total momentum after.
beats.caption: Total momentum stays the same

beats.text: Use signed velocities: right positive, left negative. The minus sign describes direction, not mass.
beats.caption: Right positive; left negative

beats.text: Find B's final velocity. Keep both diagrams beside the working.
With negligible external horizontal force, momentum before equals momentum after.
Mass A times u A, plus mass B times u B, equals mass A times v A, plus mass B times v B.
beats.ink: mA uA + mB uB = mA vA + mB vB

beats.text: Substitute: two times four, plus three times negative one, equals two times negative two, plus three v B.
Eight minus three gives five on the left. A's final momentum is negative four, leaving three v B.
Add four to both sides: nine equals three v B.
Divide by three. B's velocity is positive three metres per second: a speed of three, to the right.
The positive answer confirms our assumed arrow. A moves left, B moves right, and the particles separate.
Reset to the original incoming particles. This independent trial ends with them sticking.
The same external force condition holds, so momentum before equals momentum after.
After sticking, both have velocity v. Mass A times u A, plus mass B times u B, equals the sum of the masses, times v.
Two times four, plus three times negative one, equals two plus three, all multiplied by v.
The initial momentum is five. The combined mass is five kilograms, so five equals five v.
Divide by the combined mass. Their common velocity is positive one metre per second, so both move right together.
One common velocity replaces two separate after velocities. The particles remain in contact; their masses still add.

scenes.title: Check the system and the direction

beats.text: What if an external horizontal push mattered during impact? The pair could gain momentum; we could no longer equate the totals.
beats.caption: External push: total momentum can change

beats.text: Return to our original negligible force condition. A reverses direction. Does that mean the pair's total momentum is not conserved?
beats.caption: Does reversal break total momentum conservation?

beats.text: No. The individual momentum changes are opposite; the pair's total remains conserved.
beats.caption: Individual changes; conserved total
